summary: The paper's Results section states the MIC method. WT BW1556 is grown in two-fold serial dilutions of each drug in LB. MIC is the lowest dose with OD at 48 h below 10% of the drug-free control. Screening dose is usually MIC/2. Table 1 gives the MIC and screening concentration for all 18 compounds. The dilution-plate set-up, stock preparation and inoculum density are not described. They can be assumed from the Growth Profiler workflow in Methods without changing what is measured.

gaps.detail: Dilution series range, top concentration and number of two-fold steps per antimicrobial
gaps.why_needed: To bracket the MIC for each drug and choose the sub-inhibitory dose
gaps.resolution: Use two-fold dilutions of each drug in LB, spanning about 4-5 steps above and below the Table 1 MIC. Table 1 MICs in mg/L: azithromycin 30, cefiderocol 1, cefoperazone 0.5, chloramphenicol 2.5, ceftriaxone 2.5, D-cycloserine 12.5, gentamicin 4, levofloxacin 0.25, meropenem 0.0625, ofloxacin 0.125, ornidazole 800, phosphomycin 50, rifampicin 25, streptomycin 25, trimethoprim 2.3. Flumequine (>1.5), paraquat (>268) and zidovudine (>100) still grew at the highest dose tested, so the top concentration is the tabulated value. Paraquat growth was not fully inhibited up to 257 mg/L, but inhibition was visible at 32 mg/L (Fig 7A).
gaps.source: https://www.mdpi.com/2079-6382/11/8/1129 (Section 2.2, Table 1, paraquat text); standard practice for series design

gaps.detail: Culture volume per well, plate type and inoculation per well for the MIC plates
gaps.why_needed: Cell density and path length determine the growth curve and the MIC readout
gaps.resolution: Same format as the screen. Use CR1496c polystyrene 96-well Growth Profiler plates. Pre-load each well with 3 uL of WT overnight culture mixed 1:1 with 50% glycerol (stored at -20 C). Then add 297 uL LB containing the drug (300 uL final) and seal with CR1396b sandwich covers.
gaps.source: Paper Section 4 (Materials and Methods); the MIC-specific plate set-up is assumed to follow it

gaps.detail: Inoculum density (OD or CFU) of the WT overnight culture
gaps.resolution: Use the paper's pre-inoculated glycerol-stock procedure. Inoculate 1 mL LB from a WT glycerol stock, grow overnight at 37 C with agitation, then mix with 1 mL 50% glycerol. No OD is given, so the density is not standardised.

gaps.detail: Drug stock solvent and stock concentration
gaps.why_needed: To prepare the dilution series accurately and avoid solvent toxicity
gaps.resolution: The paper says the compounds were readily soluble in LB. Dissolve each in LB or water, or in a minimal volume of the manufacturer-recommended solvent where needed, and filter-sterilise. Prepare concentrated stocks in LB and make serial 2-fold dilutions in LB. Keep any solvent constant and low (<=1%).
gaps.source: standard practice; Section 2.1 of paper (solubility in LB)

gaps.detail: Incubation time, temperature, shaking, imaging interval
gaps.why_needed: Defines the readout used for the MIC call
gaps.resolution: MIC read at 48 h. Growth Profiler 960 at 37 C, 225 rpm, image every 20 min. G-values converted to OD600 = 0.0158*(G-Gblank)^0.9854.

gaps.detail: MIC definition and sub-inhibitory dose choice
gaps.why_needed: Criterion for calling the MIC and selecting the screening concentration
gaps.resolution: MIC is the lowest concentration with OD at 48 h below 10% of the antibiotic-free LB control. The screening concentration is generally MIC/2. A lower dose is used if growth effects (lower max OD, longer lag, slower rate) are clear at lower doses.
n = 3 for the paraquat concentration-inhibition curves (Fig 7A). Replicate numbers for the other MICs are not stated; assume triplicate.

retrieved_details: Strain: wild-type E. coli BW1556 (Keio parent strain). Medium: Lucia Broth (LB). MIC method: growth in a two-fold serial dilution of drug in LB; MIC = OD at 48 h <10% of the drug-free control; screening concentration usually MIC/2 (https://www.mdpi.com/2079-6382/11/8/1129, Section 2.2). Table 1 (WT MIC / screening conc, mg/L): azithromycin 30/7.5; cefiderocol 1/0.25; cefoperazone 0.5/0.25; chloramphenicol 2.5/1.25; ceftriaxone 2.5/1; D-cycloserine 12.5/6.25; flumequine >1.5/1.5; gentamicin 4/2; levofloxacin 0.25/0.125; meropenem 0.0625/0.03125; ofloxacin 0.125/0.0625; ornidazole 800/400; paraquat >268/67; phosphomycin 50/25; rifampicin 25/12.5; streptomycin 25/6.25; trimethoprim 2.3/0.25; zidovudine >100/100. Flumequine, paraquat and zidovudine grew at the highest concentration tested. Paraquat: growth not fully inhibited up to 257 mg/L, inhibition evident at 32 mg/L (Fig 7A, n=3). The paper is internally inconsistent: the Figure 6 legend says 400 mg/L azithromycin, but Table 1 gives a 7.5 mg/L screening dose and the text mentions 7.5 mg/L. The paraquat text says the screen used 67 mg/L, while the Fig 7 legend shows 32 mg/L curves. Antibiotics came from Sigma, except rifampicin, ceftriaxone and azithromycin from TCI. Plate format and readout: Enzyscreen CR1496c plates, 3 uL culture:50% glycerol (1:1) pre-load, 297 uL LB+drug, CR1396b sandwich cover, Growth Profiler 960 at 37 C, 225 rpm, images every 20 min; OD600=0.0158*(G-Gblank)^0.9854 (Section 4). The MIC-specific plate set-up and workflow are in Supplementary Figure S1, which was not used. The bench protocol must assume it follows the screen format.
